title: Astrid and the Salt
premise: Felix Eastwick, a charm-seller hiding her magic in the city of Greyharbor, discovers that Astrid—the woman she's been quietly falling for—is named in the Salt Codex, a century-old book of prophecies that predicts Astrid will either save or doom the last dragon-fire. The prophecy hinges on a door out of Vellmark, a country erased from maps and memory after a magical purge, and only Felix's dying guild still knows how to find it. As guild elders, inquisitors, and a corrupt minister who feeds on confiscated magic all close in, Felix must choose between protecting Astrid by lying to her and trusting her with a truth that could break them both. In the end, they open the door together—not to escape, but to carry the last dragon-fire through it and reignite the country everyone pretended never existed.
about_author: Silas Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people caught in machinery much older than themselves.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She sells a luck-charm to a dockworker, hides her guild mark from a patrol, and meets Astrid again at the night market. The beat is quiet longing under surveillance—two women performing normalcy in a city where their real selves are contraband.

chapters.title: The Book That Shouldn't Be Open
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Summoned by Elder Maren, Felix is shown the Salt Codex, its pages naming 'Astrid of the Tide-Line' as keeper-or-killer of the last flame. The emotional beat is dread: the one person Felix wanted outside history is written into it.

chapters.title: Salt on Her Lips
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid reveals she has always dreamed of a burning door and salt water; she came to Greyharbor chasing the dream. Felix says nothing about the Codex. The beat is intimacy built on a growing lie.

chapters.title: The Guild of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Tour of the dying guild: nine members left, charms failing, wards fraying. Maren explains the Door of Vellmark and why the guild was founded to guard it. Beat: grief for a legacy Felix never asked to inherit.

chapters.title: Minister Corvane's Collection
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid, a cartographer's assistant, is summoned to map the Minister's vault of confiscated magical objects—and feels one of them call her name. Beat: seduction of power, first taste of what the state does with magic.

chapters.title: What Felix Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid finds a scrap of Codex transcription in Felix's coat and confronts her; Felix lies badly. The date ends cold. Beat: the first fracture—loyalty to the guild versus truth to the woman she loves.

chapters.title: Nine Names, Eight Candles
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A guild member is taken by inquisitors; the guild's protective candle-snuff ritual fails for the first time in a century. Maren names Felix as heir. Beat: terror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Tide-Line
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Following the Codex's geography, Felix and Astrid reconcile enough to travel north together along the drowned coast where Vellmark used to be. Beat: wary partnership, love rekindling through shared purpose.

chapters.title: Maps of a Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid's cartography skill lets her read the erased borders; villages remember Vellmark only in songs. Beat: wonder and horror at how thoroughly a nation can be unwritten—and how much Astrid wants it back.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Who Weeps
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Inquisitor Hale catches up to them but hesitates—he was raised on Vellmark lullabies too. He lets them go with a warning: Corvane is coming personally. Beat: enemies revealed as fellow orphans of the erasure.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Corvane intercepts Astrid alone, offering to restore her family's erased name if she brings him the Codex and abandons Felix. Beat: temptation sharpened by old wounds; Astrid refuses, but not cleanly.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The pair find the chapel marking the Door's location, submerged at high tide, guarded by a ward keyed to guild blood. Felix cuts her palm to open it. Beat: sacrifice as proof of belonging—to the guild, and to Astrid.

chapters.title: Behind the Door
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Inside: Vellmark preserved, sunlit, frozen mid-century, the last dragon-fire burning in a lantern at its heart. Beat: awe curdling into unease—the country isn't dead, it's held, and something holds it.

chapters.title: The Warden of the Held Hour
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They meet the Warden, the guild's founder, kept alive by the flame, who reveals the prophecy's trap: the fire stays lit only while Vellmark stays hidden; opening the door fully will gutter it out. Beat: the choice reframed—there is no clean way to save both.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Maren arrives with the surviving guild and confesses the founding sin: the guild didn't guard the Door, it locked an entire country away to save itself from Corvane's predecessors. Beat: loyalty to the guild collapses into shame; Felix must decide what inheritance means now.

chapters.title: What the Fire Wants
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The flame speaks to Astrid through her dreams—it doesn't want preservation, it wants to be given back. Beat: Astrid accepts her role as keeper, choosing truth over every safe lie offered to her.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Corvane breaches the Door with inquisitors and his hoard of stolen magic, which begins devouring the held hour. Beat: siege, betrayal among the guild, Felix wounded defending the Codex.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The flame gutters; Vellmark starts to unravel around them, streets dissolving into salt. Hale switches sides; Maren dies holding the Door. Beat: climax of loss—everything they tried to preserve is being spent at once.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Last Flame
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid takes the lantern and walks into the unraveling heart of Vellmark to give the fire back to the land. Felix follows, choosing her over duty, over the guild, over survival. Beat: love against duty resolved—duty redefined as what you refuse to abandon.

chapters.title: Rekindling
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Astrid pours the flame into the land; Vellmark blazes back into being, and the returning light burns Corvane's stolen hoard to ash, unmaking his power. Beat: catharsis—the corrupting accumulation destroyed by a gift freely given.

chapters.title: A Country With Its Name Back
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Aftermath: refugees and exiles cross the open Door; Hale carries terms of peace to Greyharbor; the guild dissolves itself, its purpose fulfilled. Beat: bittersweet restoration—Felix is no longer invisible, and no longer certain she wants to be.

chapters.title: Astrid and the Salt
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, closing. On Vellmark's new coast, Astrid and Felix plant a garden where the chapel stood; the Codex's final page now shows two names, unwritten until chosen. Beat: quiet resolution—history made by hand, love chosen daily, the tide coming in clean.
